name: COAST
versions: 2020 3-tube design 0.40 mm OD (jeong2020_design); 2022 same family run under fluoroscopic path planning, ex vivo porcine aorta (ravigopal2022_fluoroscopic); 2023 larger 0.89 mm OD with 3-fibre FBG shape+force sensing (deaton2023_simultaneous); 2025 two-tube 'modified COAST', 0.35 mm outer tube, 0.66 mm Pebax sheath, joystick teleoperation (brumfiel2025_modified)
target_anatomy: cardiovascular / peripheral (aortic bifurcation phantom, paediatric carotid and arch phantoms)
devices_driven: the COAST wire itself (own nitinol-tube wire, not a commercial guidewire)
n_dof_detail: 4 actuated axes in 2020 prototype (tendon stroke X1, inner-tube position X2, outer-tube advance X3, whole-module advance X4); roll added by spur gear in 2025 version
rotation_detail: none in 2020 prototype; spur-gear roll of actuation module (2025)
device_range: 2020 prototype 188-257 mm tubes, 'shorter than a clinical wire'; handheld spooling variant takes up to 1.5 m (chavenet2026_handheld)
force_sensing: 2020: miniature force sensor on tendon tension; 2023: FBG triplet tip force, RMSE 0.005-0.027 N (bench)
validation_detail: ex vivo porcine aorta, navigation with COAST under fluoroscopic reconstruction (ravigopal2022 abstract); 2025: one qualitative teleoperated traversal of an aortic-bifurcation phantom with pulsatile flow, no success counts; 2020: phantom, no success count
key_numbers: 2020: tendon-stroke model RMSE 0.032 mm (27-37 mm bending lengths); follow-the-leader tip-to-path mean 4.53 mm (low curvature) and 14.66 mm (high curvature) in free space; 2023 shape RMSE 0.62-1.94 mm by motion type; 2025 wire buckled between introducer and actuator so insertion was hand-assisted
sim_model: analytical tendon-stroke / static model with experimental fit (jeong2020 Sec. III, full); shape-from-FBG reconstruction (deaton2023, full); no physics simulator found
sim2real_detail: none found (all control open-loop or teleoperated; no learned policy)
